To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the residual packet loss probabilities of FSP over IP multicast and MPLS are almost identical and the residual packet loss of FSP over MPLS is lower than that over IP multicast.
the packet loss probability is reduced by 20% in the MPLS networks compared to IP networks when DiffServ and FSP are adopted and when the reliable ARQ multicast strategy is used.

the packet loss probability of IP multicasting is higher in MPLS networks than in plain IP networks, and that the packet loss probabilities of IP multicast in both MPLS and plain IP networks using FSP are lower than that of plain IP multicasting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the residual packet loss probabilities in reliable homogeneous multicast networks with DiffServ and MPLS.
a new policy for DiffServ over MPLS and IP reliable multicast networks.
the residual packet loss probabilities for IP and MPLS homogeneous reliable ARQ multicast networks using the FSP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residual packet loss probabilities are lower when DiffServ is adopted in IP multicast and MPLS networks using the FSP policy than when plain IP is adopted.
, the residual packet loss in IP multicasting in MPLS networks is lower than that in plain IP multicasting when DiffServ is adopted.
the residual packet loss probabilities of IP and MPLS networks using the proposed FSP are very close.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FSP is a fair share policy that can be applied to IP and MPLS multicast networks.
the FSP policy is a better choice for IP multicasting over MPLS networks when DiffServ and ARQ are used.
the residual loss probabilities for IP and MPLS networks with FSP and ARQ is less than 10−4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MPLS networks using DiffServ can provide a better QoS and lower residual packet loss probability than plain IP networks when reliable ARQ multicasting is used.
MPLS can improve packet loss probability in DiffServ over IP reliable ARQ multicast networks.
MPLS is more efficient than plain IP in terms of residual packet loss probability.
